new: Spaceships are now steered with the right stick: left and right turn, forward dives and back climbs, as in a flight simulator. Let go and it flies level.
Tilting the controller no longer steers: how you hold it does not matter any more.
While a ship flies, a click of the right stick counts only with the stick at its middle, so a hard push that clicks does not land the ship or open the menu. Two clicks at the middle still land it.
Everything else about the ships is as in v132: launch and land with two clicks of the right stick, the grip brakes, A boosts, the trigger shoots, drones, targets and pickups shared in a room.
test: Launch with two clicks of the right stick. Do the stick's turn and climb feel right: the dead zone in the middle, how fast a full push turns, forward to dive and back to climb?
Push the stick hard and click it by accident while flying: the ship should keep flying and the menu stay shut. Two clicks with the stick at its middle should still land it.
Hold the controller at any angle while flying: the ship should not care.
The left stick clicked twice should still turn moving with the sticks on and off (VR), in the studio too.
untested: Everything on a real headset: how the stick feels and its numbers (a dead zone of 0.15, a full turn of 140 degrees a second, 60 degrees of climb), and whether 0.5 is the right point for ignoring a pushed click.
Two headsets flying together: v133 changes only how each ship is steered, but the shared room's ship round was not run again here.
On dev only the quick checks ran, with the spaceship smoke steps; the full suites run before the main site moves.
